papers.authors: Malhotra A, Gottlieb DJ, Woehrle H, Dennehy EB, Calamai G, Liu Z, Chakladar S, Grimes R et al.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common disorder characterized by repeated upper airway collapse during sleep that is associated with reduced quality of life and increased incidence of cardiometabolic disease. OBJECTIVE: To assess the effects of orforglipron on moderate to severe OSA in adults with obesity or overweight, compared with placebo. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Two 52-week, phase 3, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trials were conducted at 66 sites in the US, Argentina, Brazil, China, Czech Republic, Germany, Japan, Mexico, and Taiwan. Adults with moderate to severe OSA and body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) of 27 or higher were enrolled between November 11, 2024, and July 23, 2025. Final follow-up occurred on July 30, 2026. Trial 1 included patients not receiving positive airway pressure treatment and trial 2 included patients receiving positive airway pressure treatment. INTERVENTION: Patients were randomized (1:1) to receive either once-daily orforglipron (maximum tolerated dose: equivalent to 9-, 14.5-, or 17.2-mg tablet dose) or placebo. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was change in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, events/h) from baseline to week 52. Seven key multiplicity-controlled secondary end points included change in sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Short Form Sleep-Related Impairment T-score, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein. RESULTS: A total of 363 patients were randomized in trial 1 (mean age, 48.4 years; BMI, 37.4; AHI, 50.7 events/h; 31.4% female) and 349 patients were randomized in trial 2 (mean age, 51.1 years; BMI, 38.6; AHI, 57.6 events/h; 26.9% female). For the treatment regimen estimand, in trial 1, the mean AHI change was -17.8 for orforglipron compared with -4.5 for placebo (difference, -13.2 [95% CI, -17.7 to -8.7]; P < .001) at 52 weeks. In trial 2, the mean AHI change was -17.3 for orforglipron and -5.3 for placebo (difference, -12.0 [95% CI, -17.1 to -6.9]; P < .001) at 52 weeks. Of 7 key secondary end points, 6 were statistically significant, favoring orforglipron. Gastrointestinal events were the most commonly reported adverse events, occurring in 123 (68.0%) participants randomized to receive orforglipron vs 68 (37.4%) randomized to receive placebo in trial 1 and in 125 (70.6%) participants randomized to receive orforglipron vs 63 (36.6%) randomized to receive placebo in trial 2. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: These results provide evidence for the potential use of oral orforglipron to improve sleep-disordered breathing in adults with moderate to severe OSA and obesity or overweight. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06649045.

papers.abstract_en: Single-port robotic-assisted thoracic surgery (SP-RATS) has expanded rapidly, but its comparative effectiveness remains uncertain across platforms and access strategies. We systematically evaluated SP-RATS against multiport robotic-assisted thoracic surgery (MP-RATS) and uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (uVATS). PubMed/MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and supplementary sources were searched through October 5, 2026. Random-effects meta-analyses with modified Knapp-Hartung inference were used for continuous and common binary outcomes, whereas rare events were analyzed using fixed-effect Peto odds ratios. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and certainty using GRADE. Sixty reports were included; 23 provided Group A or B comparative data, with one study at critical risk of bias excluded from the primary quantitative synthesis. Compared with MP-RATS, SP-RATS demonstrated broadly similar perioperative outcomes without a consistent disadvantage. Lymph-node yield was nominally lower (MD, - 1.18 nodes; 95% CI, - 2.31 to - 0.05; P = 0.043), but this finding did not persist across sensitivity analyses. Compared with uVATS, SP-RATS was associated with shorter chest-tube duration (MD, - 0.49 days; 95% CI, - 0.85 to - 0.13; P = 0.013), with additional favorable signals in lymph-node yield, chest drainage, and conversion, although these were less consistent across sensitivity analyses. Complications, R0 resection, and mortality did not differ significantly between approaches. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across all pooled outcomes. SP-RATS appears to be a viable minimally invasive alternative, achieving reduced robotic access without an evident trade-off in perioperative safety or immediate oncologic outcomes. Prospective comparative studies are needed to determine whether reduced robotic access provides reproducible clinical benefit.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Adult eosinophilic asthma (EA) is a predominant phenotype of severe asthma. Induced sputum cytology, the diagnostic gold standard, is limited by complex procedures and poor feasibility. Non-invasive type 2 markers perform unsatisfactorily, and existing machine learning models lack interpretability and clinical accessibility. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to construct a machine learning (ML)-based prediction model for EA to enable accurate phenotyping and personalized precision treatment of asthma. METHODS: A single-center retrospective study was performed at a tertiary hospital in China. A total of 734 asthmatic patients who underwent induced sputum cytology were screened, and 503 were ultimately included. Data preprocessing, missing value imputation, and feature normalization were conducted within the training set to avoid data leakage. Ten ML algorithms were developed with hyperparameter tuning and internal cross-validation for model optimization. Model performance was assessed using AUC, calibration curves, DCA, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, and confusion matrix. The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was used to improve model interpretability. RESULTS: Our results showed that the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) model outperformed the other 9 ML algorithms. After feature selection, an interpretable final KNN model incorporating 6 features was developed, achieving the following performance metrics: AUC = 0.814, accuracy = 0.780, sensitivity = 0.845, specificity = 0.697, precision = 0.780, and F1-score = 0.811. Fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO50) was the most important predictor, followed by blood eosinophil count (bEOS). A web-based prediction tool with a probability threshold of 0.391 was developed for clinical use. CONCLUSION: The developed ML model holds promise as a non-invasive alternative to induced sputum cytology for EA diagnosis. The corresponding web-based prediction tool is accessible at https://mm-zhou-2026.shinyapps.io/adult-eosinophilic-asthma-prediction/ and may help clinicians achieve rapid phenotyping and personalized precision treatment for adult asthma.

papers.abstract_en: Impaired pulmonary epithelial cell homeostasis is a key pathogenic feature in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Mucin 1 (MUC1/Muc1) is a membrane-tethered glycoprotein that plays important roles in modulating various disease progression. This study aims to decipher the role and mechanisms of MUC1 in the pathogenesis of COPD. We found functional variants (rs4072037 T > C and rs12411216 C > A) in MUC1 were associated with increased susceptibility to COPD. MUC1-C expression in lung tissues was age-dependent, elevated in adults but decreased in elderly COPD patients. Aged Muc1-deficient mice showed increased cellular senescence in alveolar type II (AT2) epithelial cells and spontaneously developed emphysema. In cigarette smoke (CS)-induced COPD model mice, Muc1 deficiency caused an accelerated decline in lung function, impaired mitochondrial function, enhanced lung inflammation, and impaired AT2-to- alveolar type I (AT1) epithelial cell transdifferentiation. Adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9)-mediated AT2 cell-specific reconstitution of Muc1 ameliorated COPD in association with integrated suppression of pulmonary inflammation and enhancement of AT2 transdifferentiation and mitochondrial function. Mechanistically, we found MUC1 attenuated senescence and associated cell dysfunction, including activation of PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy flux and AMPK/NDUFS4-driven mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming in AT2 cells. In addition, MUC1 modulated CS extract (CSE)-induced human AT2-to-AT1 transdifferentiation through enhancement of β-catenin nuclear translocation. Moreover, overexpression of MUC1 in lung epithelial cells inhibited CS-induced NF-κB activation and inflammatory responses in both in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, this study identified MUC1 as a protective molecule and potential target for COPD, particularly emphysema, via facilitating AT2-to-AT1 cell transdifferentiation, while prohibiting senescence and inflammation.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Neighborhood social disadvantage (NSD) is increasingly recognized as being associated with health disparities. However, its associations with longitudinal lung function decline, health-related quality of life (HRQOL), and mortality remain incompletely understood. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations of NSD with lung function, HRQOL, and all-cause mortality and to explore potential mediators of any association. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prospective cohort study of current and former smokers aged 40 to 75 years with at least 10 pack-years of smoking history in the Lovelace Smokers Cohort. Participants underwent repeated spirometry approximately every 18 months from 2001 through 2017. Mortality was ascertained through October 2020 using the National Death Index. Data were analyzed from January to May 2025. EXPOSURES: Census tract-level Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) and Social Deprivation Index (SDI) assigned to residential addresses. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Baseline and longitudinal lung function (forced expiratory volume in 1 second [FEV1], forced vital capacity [FVC], and the FEV1:FVC ratio), baseline HRQOL assessed by the St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ), with higher scores indicating poorer respiratory health status, and the 36-item Short Form Survey, and all-cause mortality. Formal mediation analyses evaluated educational attainment, current smoking status, and dietary patterns, whereas baseline lung function and HRQOL were considered as potential mediators for associations of NSD with all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Among 2362 included participants, the mean (SD) baseline age was 56.3 (9.4) years, and 1738 (73.58%) were female. A 1-IQR increase in SDI was associated with lower baseline FEV1 (β, -0.09 [95% CI, -0.13 to -0.06] L) and FEV1:FVC ratio (β, -1.21 [95% CI, -1.80 to -0.62] percentage points). Higher SVI was associated with faster annual decline in FEV1 (β, -3.11 [95% CI, -5.86 to -0.36] mL/y) and FEV1:FVC ratio (β, -0.05 [95% CI, -0.11 to -0.001] percentage points/y), worse baseline HRQOL, including a higher SGRQ total score (β, 4.46 [95% CI, 3.26-5.65] points), and higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.08-1.53]). Current smoking status and 2 dietary pattern scores mediated 4.4% (95% CI, -1.2% to 12.8%) to 31.0% (95% CI, 13.0%-51.6%) and 4.5% (95% CI, 0.2%-12.9%) to 17.0% (95% CI, 5.5%-113.7%), respectively, of selected associations between NSD and lung health outcomes; baseline lung function and HRQOL mediated 6.7% (95% CI, 0.6%-22.8%) to 38.6% (95% CI, 19.9%-125.3%) of selected associations with all-cause mortality. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study, worse NSD was associated with faster lung function decline, worse HRQOL, and higher all-cause mortality among ever smokers. Mediation analyses suggested that current smoking status and dietary patterns may partially account for associations of NSD with lung function and HRQOL.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Computed tomography (CT)-based noninvasive prediction of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutation status in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is highly important for advancing precision diagnosis and treatment. Current detection methods that rely on invasive tissue biopsies present several limitations. This study aimed to develop a model that integrated deep learning and multimodal information for the noninvasive prediction of EGFR-sensitizing mutations (exon 19 deletion and L858R point mutation) in NSCLC patients using contrast-enhanced CT (CE-CT) images. METHODS: We retrospectively included 466 pathologically confirmed NSCLC patients from two centers (413 from our own center for model development and internal validation, and 53 from another center for independent external validation), and proposed a novel paradigm combining disentangled self-supervised learning (D-SSL) with multimodal gated fusion. The D-SSL encoder was pretrained on CT images and tumor ROI masks from the entire 413-patient internal cohort without using EGFR mutation labels and was subsequently fixed for downstream classification. An adaptive gated fusion network was subsequently constructed to dynamically integrate these deep features with traditional radiomics features and clinical information to predict the EGFR-sensitizing mutation status. RESULTS: In 20 repeated random splits, the D-SSL fusion models achieved mean AUCs of 0.800 (±0.052) and 0.794 (±0.048) on the training set and internal test set, respectively. One-way ANOVA and subsequent Tukey HSD post-hoc test revealed that the performance on the internal test set of the D-SSL fusion models was significantly superior to that of the clinical models, radiomics models, and radiomics-clinical fusion models (all p < 0.001). On the fully independent external validation set, which was not involved in D-SSL pretraining or downstream model development, the D-SSL fusion models maintained robust performance with a mean AUC of 0.680 (±0.038). Ablation studies showed that models using only the shape head or only the texture head achieved mean AUCs of 0.680 (±0.023) and 0.684 (±0.028), respectively, both significantly lower than that of the complete D-SSL fusion models (both p < 0.001), confirming the complementarity of shape and texture features. Subgroup analysis demonstrated that the model achieved accuracies significantly above the random chance level (50%) in female 83.65% (±3.97%), male 68.90% (±3.72%), smoker 85.07% (±4.41%), and nonsmoker 69.21% (±3.44%) subgroups, suggesting that it did not merely rely on clinical features but captured deep imaging phenotypes associated with EGFR-sensitizing mutations. Feature visualization analysis demonstrated that the D-SSL feature space could effectively distinguish among various imaging manifestation types and pathological categories, confirming the model's ability to capture highly discriminative and clinically meaningful imaging phenotypes. CONCLUSIONS: This study developed a framework integrating D-SSL and multimodal fusion for the noninvasive prediction of EGFR-sensitizing mutations in NSCLC. The framework demonstrated strong discrimination in the internal transductive evaluation and retained predictive value in a fully independent external cohort. These findings support the potential of self-supervised representation learning and gated multimodal fusion, while larger multicenter studies using strictly inductive split-before-pretraining designs remain necessary.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses are major contributors to population mortality, but cause-of-death coding undercounts their impact. Ecological regression linking viral circulation to mortality fluctuations can address this. We estimated the population attributable fraction (PAF) of mortality associated with influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in Ontario, Canada, over 1993-2025, across the pandemic transition. METHODS: We analysed monthly all-cause mortality with laboratory surveillance indicators for influenza A, influenza B, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2. Negative binomial models with secular trends, Fourier seasonal terms, and population offsets were fitted for pre-pandemic (1993-2020) and combined pandemic (2020-2025) periods. PAFs were derived from counterfactual predictions. Further analyses examined temporal stratification, exclusion of the early pandemic period, and models without Fourier adjustment. FINDINGS: Pre-pandemic, influenza A was associated with 1.8% (95% CI 1.4-2.3) of mortality; influenza B showed no association; RSV showed positive associations (1.9%, 1.3-2.4) only without seasonal adjustment. Amid elevated pandemic mortality (IRR 1.052, p < 0.0001), SARS-CoV-2 was associated with 6.48% (4.5-8.4) of deaths, 3-4-fold the pre-pandemic influenza A burden. Attributable deaths (18,052) fell within 3% of 18,594 independently adjudicated Ontario COVID-19 deaths. Post-Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) SARS-CoV-2 mortality (9.8%, 1.1-17.7) did not differ from PHEIC estimates; post-PHEIC influenza did not differ from pre-pandemic baselines. INTERPRETATION: SARS-CoV-2 was associated with a 3-4-fold higher population mortality burden than seasonal influenza A despite available countermeasures, and continued to contribute beyond the formal emergency period, underscoring the importance of sustained respiratory virus prevention. papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To evaluate associations of genetically predicted plasma lipid metabolites and immune-cell phenotypes with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and assess candidate immune-mediated lipid-COPD pathways. METHODS: We conducted two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses using genome-wide association study summary statistics for COPD in 458,440 individuals of European ancestry (26,274 cases and 432,166 controls), 179 plasma lipid metabolites in 7,174 Finnish participants, and 731 immune-cell phenotypes in 3,757 Sardinian participants. Genetic instruments selected at P<1×10-5 were linkage-disequilibrium clumped, harmonized and screened for instrument strength. Inverse-variance weighting (IVW) was the primary estimator, with robust adjusted profile score (MR-RAPS) used for sensitivity analysis. Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction was applied separately across the complete lipid and immune-cell test families. Reverse MR of 13 selected lipids, cross-ancestry analyses using an East-Asian COPD outcome, and two-step MR of 18 previously selected candidate pathways were exploratory. Indirect effects were estimated, and complementary multivariable MR with conditional F-statistics were evaluated separately; BH correction covered the reverse and indirect-effect families. RESULTS: Twenty-one lipid metabolites and 48 immune-cell phenotypes showed nominal IVW associations with COPD (P<0.05), however, none met the complete-family threshold of q<0.05. Six immune-cell phenotypes reached an exploratory (q<0.10) threshold. MR-RAPS estimates were generally directionally consistent with the European IVW estimates but did not identify any complete-family (q<0.05) associations. The cross-ancestry outcome analysis did not consistently support the focused European signals. None of the 18 indirect effects survived BH correction. For the pathway from phosphatidylcholine (16:0_20:4) to COPD through CD62L- myeloid dendritic cell absolute count, the indirect effect was 0.0037 (95% CI -0.0008 to 0.0083; P=0.110; BH q=0.138). Two reverse-MR associations were nominally significant, but neither survived correction across 13 tests (both BH q=0.140). Although multivariable MR identified several direct-effect patterns within the selected candidate set, these findings did not establish mediation. CONCLUSION: The primary European analyses provided limited evidence for multiplicity-adjusted associations of the evaluated plasma lipid metabolites or immune-cell phenotypes with COPD, and none of the candidate indirect effects was statistically supported. Reverse-MR signals should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and require validation in independent cohorts and experimental studies. The present findings do not support clinical risk prediction or diagnostic application.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Evidence that multiplex polymerase chain reaction (mPCR) improves antimicrobial therapy and clinical outcomes in the critical care setting is limited. We assessed the impact of rapid mPCR on antibiotic therapy in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients with suspected pneumonia. METHODS: IRISPAT-1 was a single center, randomized, controlled open-label trial designed to determine the feasibility, safety, and potential impact of rapid respiratory pathogen detection on antibiotic therapy in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients with suspected pneumonia. Mechanically ventilated adults with suspected pneumonia and treated with new antibiotics within 24 h were randomized to standard care or mPCR using BioFire® FilmArray® Pneumonia Panel in addition to standard care (FA Pneumonia Panel group). Primary outcome was time interval (hours) to appropriate antimicrobial therapy. RESULTS: Forty mechanically ventilated patients with suspected pneumonia were randomized (20 = standard care, 20 = FA Pneumonia Panel) between July 7, 2024 and October 4, 2025. Median (IQR) time to appropriate antibiotic therapy was shorter in the FA Pneumonia Panel group compared to the standard care group (7 [5-16] vs. 72 [41-140] hours, HR 3.3; 95%CI [1.6, 6.6], p = 0.001). Adherence to treatment algorithm was observed in 90% (18/20) of patients in the FA Pneumonia Panel group. There were no differences in use of broad-spectrum antibiotics, duration of antibiotics, ventilator free days or vasopressor free days and 28-day mortality between treatment groups. CONCLUSION: Rapid mPCR with high adherence to antibiotic algorithms shortened time to appropriate antibiotics compared to standard care in mechanically ventilated patients with suspected pneumonia. papers.abstract_en: Influenza A virus (IAV) pandemics can arise when animal-derived and human-adapted IAVs exchange genome segments; however, whether contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses can generate viable reassortants with human IAVs is unclear. Here, we tested the reassortment potential of two clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses with human-adapted H1N1 and H3N2 IAVs using a biosafe reassortment system. Across multiple coinfection conditions, we genotyped 2,698 plaque-purified viral clones and recovered 20 reassortants (0.74%). Polymerase assays identified human IAV subunits, particularly H1N1 PA or H3N2 PB2, that increased H5N1 polymerase activity. Thus, contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses can reassort with human IAVs, but factors beyond polymerase compatibility may limit their recovery.

papers.abstract_en: This study developed and validated a digital twin of patient flow and waiting list dynamics in a Sleep-Disordered Breathing Unit, based on a discrete-event simulation (DES) model in the context of growing diagnostic demand mainly driven by obstructive sleep apnoea. The stochastic model, implemented in MATLAB, reproduces six care stages (e-Consultation, face-to-face consultation, overnight pulse oximetry, respiratory polygraphy, polysomnography and follow-up consultation), using operational data from year 2024 for parameterisation and data from year 2025 for correlation and validation. Key performance indicators included mean waiting time and mean queue length per stage, with model fidelity assessed via Mean Absolute Error, Root Mean Squared Error and Relative Percent Difference (RPD), both by stage and globally across the full patient pathway. The model accurately reproduced the aggregate system workload, with a weighted RPD of 3.6% for mean queue length and 34.6% for mean waiting time. Respiratory polygraphy showed the best agreement in terms of service load (RPD 2.7%), whereas the follow-up consultation exhibited the largest discrepancies in waiting times (RPD 73.7%), likely related to prioritisation rules and organisational variability not explicitly modelled. Overall, this digital twin provides an operationally useful representation to support 'what-if' analyses of organisational scenarios aimed at reducing diagnostic delays, representing one of the first validated applications of DES model in a dedicated Sleep-Disordered Breathing Unit and provides a basis for future applications incorporating urgency stratification and prospective analysis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic respiratory infections caused by pathogens including Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa) pose a major therapeutic challenge in patients with pulmonary diseases such as cystic fibrosis (CF) and non-CF bronchiectasis, where treatment efficacy is limited by the formation of biofilms, the emergence of multidrug resistant pathogens and a shortage of new and effective antibiotic classes. One approach to address this problem involves the use of "antibiotic enhancers", which are compounds that potentiate the activity of existing antibiotics without possessing direct antimicrobial effects of their own. The mucoactive thiol-based prodrug erdosteine, currently approved for the treatment of acute and chronic respiratory diseases, has been reported to exhibit anti-adhesive activity against respiratory pathogens, suggesting a clinically relevant contribution to the prevention of bacterial colonisation. Furthermore, in addition to reported anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, erdosteine has demonstrated the ability to potentiate the activity of various antimicrobial drugs. However, to date, whether erdosteine can enhance the activity of tobramycin, an antibiotic widely used to treat pathogens in the respiratory tract, has not been investigated. In this study, we investigated the ability of MET-1, the primary active metabolite of erdosteine, to enhance the activity of tobramycin against P. aeruginosa strains using a panel of both in vitro and in vivo assays. METHODS: The activity of both mono- and combination therapies was measured in planktonic P. aeruginosa (strains RP73 & PAO1) using in vitro microdilution assays including chequerboard analysis and time-kill assays, whilst activity against biofilms were analysed using microtiter plate assays with readouts including total biomass, metabolic activity, and bacterial enumeration. Combination therapy of 40 mg/kg tobramycin and 100 mg/kg erdosteine was also assessed in vivo using a murine model of chronic pulmonary infection induced by P. aeruginosa. RESULTS: 10 mg/L MET-1 significantly enhanced the antimicrobial activity of tobramycin in planktonic cultures of RP73 at 24 h and PAO1 at 4 h, leading to a greater than 2 log10 reduction in bacterial numbers compared to tobramycin monotherapy, despite MET-1 demonstrating no intrinsic bactericidal activity. In mature biofilms, MET-1 substantially enhanced tobramycin activity, reducing the biomass-derived IC₅₀ by approximately 18-fold in RP73 and 13-fold in PAO1. Finally, combination therapy of 40 mg/kg tobramycin and 100 mg/kg erdosteine was associated with a lower pulmonary bacterial burden in a murine model of chronic pulmonary infection. CONCLUSIONS: Our in vitro and in vivo studies highlight the ability of erdosteine to potentiate the activity of tobramycin suggesting that erdosteine has the potential to reduce the burden of long-term antimicrobial therapies in patients with chronic respiratory infections and thus improve clinical outcomes.

papers.title_zh: 各国国家结核病指南的全球差异：范围综述——诊断与治疗方案总体与WHO标准一致，但病例发现、LTBI管理、治疗监测与HIV/TB整合存在显著差异
papers.title_en: Global Variation in National Tuberculosis Guidelines: A Scoping Review.
papers.authors: Chin K, Foo JY, Low SG, Ong CY
papers.affiliation_highlight: Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore.
papers.results: 纳入76份指南文件，来自34个国家和国际组织。核心临床实践（如诊断和治疗方案）与WHO标准总体高度一致；在病例发现策略、潜伏结核感染（LTBI）管理、治疗监测和HIV/TB服务整合方面存在显著差异。高发病率国家优先采取主动病例发现以减少传播，低发病率国家强调针对性筛查和预防治疗。摘要未报告任何比例、效应量、一致性指标或CI/P值。
papers.authors_conclusion: 尽管结核病的临床管理已大体标准化，指南实施的差异反映了流行病学与资源可及性的不同；解决结构性障碍并支持因地制宜的实施，将是优化结核病防控、改善不同场景下结局的关键。
papers.ai_note: 范围综述，摘要未报告纳入指南的质量评价或偏倚风险评估，也未说明是否遵循PRISMA-ScR、是否注册方案或双人独立筛选，信息不足；'高度一致''显著差异'等核心判断未给出量化比例（如各领域一致的指南数/百分比），无法核验；仅覆盖34个国家，占全球国家比例及国家选择方式信息不足；数据库名称与灰色文献检索策略细节信息不足。摘要以'临床管理已大体标准化'的正面框架收尾，与同段并列的'显著差异'并存，存在选择性强调倾向。

pico.p: 2015–2025年发表的76份国家与国际结核病指南文件，来自34个国家和国际组织
pico.ic: 按WHO发病率阈值划分的高发病率与低发病率国家指南，在筛查、诊断、治疗、预防治疗、治疗监测、HIV/TB合并感染等领域的内容比较（无干预-对照设计）

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading cause of infectious mortality worldwide, with primary care playing a central role in early detection, treatment, and prevention. The World Health Organization (WHO) End TB Strategy provides a global framework for TB control, but its implementation varies across national guidelines. METHODS: We conducted a scoping review of national and international TB guidelines published between 2015 and 2025. A systematic search of databases and grey literature identified relevant documents. Guidelines were analysed across key domains of TB management, including screening, diagnosis, treatment, preventive therapy, treatment monitoring, and HIV/TB coinfection. Countries were classified as high- or low-incidence settings based on WHO incidence thresholds. RESULTS: 76 guideline documents from 34 countries and international organisations were included. Overall, strong alignment with WHO standards was observed for core clinical practices such as diagnosis and treatment regimens. However, substantial variation was identified in case-finding strategies, latent TB infection (LTBI) management, treatment monitoring, and HIV/TB service integration. High-incidence countries prioritised active case finding to reduce transmission, whereas low-incidence countries emphasised targeted screening and preventive therapy. CONCLUSIONS: While clinical management of TB is broadly standardised, variation in guideline implementation reflects differences in epidemiology and resource availability. Addressing structural barriers and supporting context-specific implementation will be essential to optimise TB control and improve outcomes across diverse settings.
